standard_prerequisites.name: Completion of a finite extension of Noetherian complete local rings is a product of completions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension}, cited at proof lines 12514-12515
standard_prerequisites.use: Rewrites the tensor product with L as a product of the completions of B[x] at the primes over q.

standard_prerequisites.name: A derivation of a ring extends to a localisation and to a completion
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the derivation d/dx act on the completed localisation tensored with K, where it sends x - f to a unit.

standard_prerequisites.name: Formal smoothness of the localisation at a maximal ideal and of its completion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemmas \ref{lemma-formally-smooth} and \ref{lemma-formally-smooth-completion}, cited at proof lines 12539-12541
standard_prerequisites.use: Identify the ring tensored with K as formally smooth over A, hence regular.

standard_prerequisites.name: A formally smooth algebra over a field is regular, and a quotient of a regular ring by a nonzerodivisor is regular
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Proposition \ref{proposition-fs-regular} and Lemma \ref{lemma-quotient-regular}, cited at proof lines 12542 and 12544
standard_prerequisites.use: Give regularity of the quotient by x - f, which is the ring whose geometric regularity is claimed.

core_obligations: Construct, for a finite purely inseparable extension L of the residue field, a finite extension A to B of Noetherian complete local domains with the tensor product of the residue field with B surjecting onto L (proof lines 12505-12511).

Identify the tensor product with L as a product of completed localisations of B[x] at the primes over q, reducing the claim to finiteness of the number of factors and regularity of each (proof lines 12512-12520).
Reduce to the case where the fraction field of A equals the residue field of r (proof lines 12521-12522).
In the reduced case, describe the prime rK[x] as generated by a linear polynomial x - f and write the ring as a quotient of the completed localisation tensored with K (proof lines 12524-12533).
Prove regularity of that quotient: extend the derivative to the completed localisation, use formal smoothness over A, and apply the quotient-by-a-nonzerodivisor lemma (proof lines 12534-12549).
proof_roadmap: Realise a purely inseparable test extension by a finite extension of complete local domains (proof lines 12505-12511).
Decompose the tensor product and reduce to the equal-field case (proof lines 12512-12522).
Compute the reduced case as a quotient by a linear polynomial (proof lines 12524-12533).
Conclude regularity from formal smoothness plus the derivation argument (proof lines 12534-12549).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a certain ring obtained from a completed localisation of a polynomial algebra becomes geometrically regular after extending scalars to the residue field of a prime lying over zero. The proof first uses finiteness of the fraction field extension to build, for any finite purely inseparable extension of that residue field, a finite extension of Noetherian complete local domains realising it, then rewrites the tensor product as a product of completed localisations of the extended polynomial algebra and reduces to the case where the residue field is the fraction field itself. In that case the prime ideal is principal, the ring is exhibited as a quotient by a linear polynomial, and regularity follows from formal smoothness of the completed localisation together with an explicit derivation that maps the linear polynomial to a unit. The reduction and the final computation are both carried out in the author's text.
